newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire official says army still holds Kindu.
newsitem.headline: Zaire official says army still holds Kindu.

text.p: A Zairean official said the eastern town of Kindu remained in army hands on Friday, dismissing reports that rebels had captured it as a ploy.
The defence ministry official told Reuters that Kindu, a well-fortified transport hub and base for army operations in the war zone, was quiet at midday on Friday.
"Kindu has not fallen. That information is baseless," he said. "Kindu was calm up until noon (1100 GMT), the last time we contacted the people there."
The official said that the rebels were not at Kindu but were 50 km (30 miles) to the east near Kalima, which they captured last weekend.
"The rebel strategy consists of announcing the fall of such and such a town before it happens," he added. "The aim of the manoeuvre is to sow panic and confusion so they can capture it easily."
Earlier, a U.N. source told Reuters in Nairobi that Kindu and its airport fell on Thursday.
He also said that relief groups had ordered the evacuation of foreign workers from Tingi Tingi refugee camp on the road to Kisangani to the north east on fears of an attack there.
Kisangani is headquarters of army operations in the war zone.
The rebels, who took up arms in October, control towns and territory in the east and have been pushing west since the army launched a much-heralded counter-offensive on January 20.
The Zairean official acknowledged that there had been panic and looting in Kindu on Thursday but said civilians not soldiers were to blame.
Zaire's rag-tag army, its soldiers traditionally poorly paid if at all, has a reputation for looting civilians in its path.
"The soldiers at Kindu are well disciplined. They did not take part in the looting but stopped it," the official said.
He had no immediate comment on the Tingi Tingi report.
President Nelson Mandela, who is trying to bring the two sides together, had talks in South Africa this week with rebel leader Laurent Kabila and an adviser to Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko.
The Organisation of African Unity on Friday called a summit on the crisis in Central Africa's volatile Great Lakes region for March 26 in Togo's capital Lome.
